chunk_map.heading: Pick one threat, record the decision (H1/lede)
Phase 1: Run the threat scan across your mapped surface
Read the threat list, expect more than you'll use
Phase 2: Pick the one threat worth hardening against
Push back on the incident story, land the mitigation
Phase 3: Write the decision as an ADR
Read the ADR, check the voice and the lens
Ask whether the ADR loads into future sessions
Save the map and the STRIDE walk before you clear

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a slide leaning on a referent never named strands the reader mid-deck. Checked every pronoun/demonstrative/named-thing per chunk against prior-chunk history. Closest candidates: chunk 0 line 7 'the map you built' and chunk 1 line 22 'the access-surface map from Exercise 1' both resolve — 'Exercise 1' ('Map the access surface') is the immediately preceding exercise in earn-the-trust.md's Start here list, and the session-artifact carve-out covers a live map the student's own Ex1 session produced. Chunk 6 line 63 'The Decision section' and line 64 'the Alternatives considered section' resolve against chunk 5's fenced prompt (line 58: 'Context / Decision / Consequences / Alternatives considered') — fences are exempt from scoring but still render on the slide, so the naming is visible prior context. Chunk 7 line 68 'the M3 worktree' is self-explanatory within its own chunk (line 69 unpacks it in the same breath: 'M3 forked a worktree at turn 1...'), and 'worktree' is independently pre-established by the module's What You'll Learn (earn-the-trust.md line 22: 'Fork a sibling git worktree'), which per rule 1's module-include-order clause counts as prior context. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found.

Harm: pointing at another file by position only works if the deck starts where the writer assumed. Chunk 1 line 22 'the access-surface map from Exercise 1' names the source by title AND unpacks its claim ('access-surface map') in the same sentence, matching the passing pattern in the rule's own example. No file is pointed at as 'above'/'the previous file' without naming. Fenced-block phrase 'path is earlier in this scrollback' (in the {{prompt}} content) is exempt from scoring.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a stranded callback sends the student hunting for a beat that was cut. Checked backward refs: 'the map you built' / 'Exercise 1' -> earn-the-trust.md line 37 '[Exercise: Map the access surface]' exists directly before this file in the module's Start here list. 'the side-quest' (chunk 7, line 68-70) -> earn-the-trust.md line 33 '[Exercise: Open the side quest]' exists as the module's first exercise. Both beats verified present in the current module file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a guess/predict beat whose answer is narrated above it teaches nothing. Only ask-then-reveal shape in the file is chunk 8: the ask ('Ask Claude whether this ADR rides into future sessions automatically', line 74) precedes the reveal ('Claude's answer: no...', line 78) in reading order. No guess-before-outcome inversion found anywhere else in the file.

Harm: a slide that says nothing standalone. Closest candidate: chunk 4 ('Push back on the incident story, land the mitigation', lines 44-47) is short (2 bullets, no prompt fence) but carries two self-carrying claims (the incident story's role, and the save-as-ADR next step), not a bare wait-state. Every chunk carries at least one self-carrying claim or a prompt fence.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts misleads a skimming reader. Checked each of the 9 `##` headers against its chunk body; each states what the chunk does (e.g. chunk 7 'Check where the ADR landed' -> body checks the ADR's save path against main repo vs. worktree). Closest to a stretch: chunk 6 'Read the ADR, check the voice and the lens' covers both a voice-check bullet and a STRIDE-fit bullet; both are legitimately 'the lens' the header promises. No contradiction found.

Harm: cadence tics read as machine-authored on a slide. Checked all five sub-items: (a) 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' banned triple construction -- not found; closest is chunk 3 line 36 'One threat, not five' which is a single contrast, not the banned three-part shape. (b) anaphora/epistrophe triples -- none found. (c) self-grading superlatives -- none found (no 'one of the most useful' phrasing anywhere in body). (d) number+retraction -- none found (no numeric claim followed by hedging). (e) abstraction-noun stacks -- none found; vocabulary stays concrete ('the access surface', 'the incident story', 'the ADR'). (f) verb triplets with an empty leg -- none found. All PASS, aggregated into this one rule-7 entry per the completeness contract.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: repo/authorial vocabulary a room can't parse. Closest candidate: 'access surface' / 'the mapped surface' recurs (chunk 0 line 7, chunk 1 heading and lines 19-20). This is standard security-engineering vocabulary (cf. 'attack surface'), not repo-internal dialect like 'compendium' or 'writing surface' -- the rule's own carve-out distinguishes domain-standard 'surface' usage from authorial jargon. No 'compendium', 'firing', 'forcing function', 'beat', or 'mood' found as internal-dialect nouns in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: over-bolding trains readers to ignore bold as a signal. All bold in body is widget/label chrome exempted by the file's own maintainer note (line 95: 'widget/label chrome ... untouched, per check_slides.md §9'): chunk 0's **Time:**/**Window:**/**What you do:**/**What you build:**/**The point:**, chunk 9's **Worth keeping?**/**What happened:**/**What this sets up:**. No bolded whole-sentence leads found in any bullet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content -- verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: content invisible in the deck gets rules 1-9 applied to a slide that never renders. This is a standard exercise file included via a plain [Exercise: ...](exercises/threat-model-with-stride.md) link in earn-the-trust.md's Start here section (line 39) -- the standard exercise-include pattern that reaches the composed deck via `.phase--exercise`/`section.module` wrapping (per `curriculum/CLAUDE.md` Directory + Classroom delivery). No phase-less bare prose section found. Mechanical checks below (rules 11/12/14) all ran successfully against this file, which would fail/error on an unreachable file, corroborating presence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering -- position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js curriculum/exercises/threat-model-with-stride.md` -> exit 0, output 'OK -- 61 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.' Phase headers in body (Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 3) are consecutive from 1 with no gaps.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js curriculum/exercises/threat-model-with-stride.md` -> exit 0, output 'OK -- 61 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' Manually confirmed no 'below/above/further down/at the top of this page' phrasing in body; the fenced-prompt phrase 'earlier in this scrollback' (chunk 1) is exempt as fenced content.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No in-body markdown links present in this file's body (only the structural include-link from the module file points at it, which is out of this file's scope). Rule is explicitly a review surface, never a gate, per the rule's own text.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size -- 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/threat-model-with-stride.md` -> output 'files: 1  slides: 9  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets... oversized: 0... every slide is within limits.' No maintainer accept-note needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a declarative heading inside an exercise where none is earned muddies the imperative/phase-label mood exercises need. Checked all 9 `##` headings: 3 are 'Phase N: <label>' (phase labels) and 6 are imperative verb phrases ('Read the threat list...', 'Push back on...', 'Read the ADR...', 'Check where...', 'Ask whether...', 'Save the map...'). None is a bare declarative claim (contrast with the compendium's own cited exceptions in close-the-ticket.md / fix-tests-first.md). Consistent exercise mood throughout.
